events.excerpt: Meta’s Ray-Ban smart glasses have attracted plenty of controversy in the relatively short time they have been available, given their potential for covert and unvanted surveillance. But given the chance to examine one it would be churlish to pass up on the opportunity to test its defences. Which is what [p0pcycle] did when the opportunity came her way . Given that hardware-probing was not an option, she followed the course of intercepting a software update. A little app decompilation led her to the full firmware, and she was able to probe its secrets. There’s a developer mode allowing applications to be written for the glasses, and it takes the form of an APK that loads the application code. An early firmware version would trust self-signed apps, so she could get arbitrary code on the device. From there after some trial and error she was able to expose a network listener, and there she had it. The write-up is an interesting walkthrough of the process, and ends with her reporting it through their bug bounty program. So sadly the steps outlined above won’t work on newer firmwares, but we’re guessing that won’t stop others probing this device further.
events.headline: Hacking Meta’s Smart Glasses

Ethereum's next upgrade debate is becoming a question of how much engineering effort should move toward long-term security. In a November 11 proposal , Ethlabs argues for making quantum protection and resilience against advanced AI-assisted attacks the priority for 2027. The practical question is which improvements can share an upgrade without slowing the security work. That trade-off deserves attention even from readers who never run a validator: protocol roadmaps influence the software that wallets, exchanges and applications must eventually support. A timetable that still needs agreement Ethlabs distinguishes basic readiness from full performance: keeping Ethereum operational with quantum-safe options is the main objective, while matching full network capacity is the more ambitious goal. Its proposed reshuffle includes withdrawing quick slots from Hegotá and reconsidering work outside that security objective. This is a contribution to Ethereum's development process. events.excerpt: Linked issue or supporting maintainer Fixes #202895 Supported by @rtimpe BC-breaking? No Summary Calling len() on a 0-dimensional tensor under torch.compile previously leaked an internal IndexError during Dynamo tracing instead of matching PyTorch eager's TypeError . This prevented standard try...except TypeError exception handling in user code and caused compilation to fail. Root Cause TensorVariable.sq_length_impl ( torch/_dynamo/variables/tensor.py ) unconditionally traced size(0) . For 0-d tensors, _method_size_stride indexed an empty size tuple, causing an internal IndexError during tracing. Fix Updated TensorVariable.sq_length_impl to check ndim . When ndim is known to be 0 , Dynamo now explicitly raises TypeError("len() of a 0-d tensor") to match eager Tensor.__len__ . If ndim is unknown, existing behavior is preserved. Test Plan Added unit tests to TestTensorLen in test/dynamo/test_len_protocol.py covering len() , __len__ , and Tensor.__len__ on 0-d tensors, try/except handling with and without fullgraph=True , and uncaught error paths. python test/dynamo/test_len_protocol.py -k TestTensorLen Pull Request resolved: #203515 Approved by: https://github.com/rtimpe

events.excerpt: An American AI lab has re-educated Qwen3.8-27B, a popular open-weight large language model from Alibaba, so the software forgets its Chinese ancestry. Nous Research, an Austin, Texas-based AI lab, has subjected the model to re-education through training, not to be confused with China's " Re-education Through Labor " system. With the help of a post-training process, Qwen3.8-27B has been reborn under the name Arete "to reinforce Western values on a Chinese-trained model." What qualifies as a "Western value" remains open to interpretation. "Open-weight Chinese models are among the strongest available, but they ship with state-aligned behavior baked into the weights," Nous Research wrote in a blog post . Your correspondent tested this with a variant model, Qwen3.8-27B-MLX-6bit, locally. Asked about events during 1989 in Tiananmen Square, the model either refused to discuss the topic or provided euphemistic response. What's perhaps more surprising is that Anthropic claims operators affiliated with Alibaba's Qwen lab used outputs from its Claude models to train competing AI models via distillation . events.excerpt: Author: Daemon Minwar Category: Economics / Mechanism Design TL;DR We propose WARCoin , a deterministic, exploit-resistant 1:1 USD stablecoin architecture designed to eliminate infinite-mint bugs, cross-collateral contagion, and replay vectors. Instead of monolithic balance mappings, WARCoin enforces a USD-only ingress firewall , burn-on-egress serial invalidation , and 7 daily color-coded ring buckets ( 1,000 serials/bucket, #1 – #1,000 ) bounded by a strict 10^9 global supply invariant. 1. Threat Model & Motivation Standard ERC-20 stablecoins rely on unbounded integer storage slots ( mapping(address => uint256) ). If a minting authority is compromised or a bridge/collateral contract is exploited, attackers can mint arbitrary unbacked supply or contaminate reserves with toxic collateral. WARCoin mitigates these vectors at the state-transition level by enforcing finite, serialized issuance slots and strict asset isolation. 2. Core Protocol Architecture A. Ingress / Egress Asset Firewall Strict USD-Only Ingress: The minting router reverts on any non-USD asset deposit ( require(asset == USD) ). External crypto-assets are rejected at the gateway to prevent collateral contagion. Burn-on-Egress Invalidation: Outbound transfers or swaps into external tokens immediately burn the underly

Yet Visa’s Trust Index found that only 23% of US consumers trust GenAI to handle payment transactions on their behalf. Well, to be clear, it is not active right now on mainnet, it requires ratification of this supported governance proposal , and this mostly serves as a way to justify it. The ZIPs are not new; they have been proposed for several years already, and one isn’t even a ZIP, just a misclarified feature. Further, ratifying does not add any new scripting or attack surface to (shielded) Zcash at all; the only change that does affect the shielded pool is respecting locktimes. How does it work? It is very complicated, but essentially, via preFROST (a modified version of FROST), it is possible to form a “covenant” such that a merchant and you can agree on terms of a subscription that are mutually enforced on-chain. events.excerpt: We continue to share monthly updates on the work behind GitHub’s availability and reliability. The short version of October: we added substantial independently scalable Azure capacity and removed several ways that failures could escalate. However, write outages, monitoring gaps during data migrations, and a regional network disruption reinforced the need for capacity growth to be paired with safer operations, stronger isolation, and validated regional recovery. As of November 9, 140 of 151 production services and 32 of 50 MySQL primaries were running in Azure Central US. Azure served 63% of migrated-service reads, 66% of monolith reads, and 52% of Git reads. We also completed a compute expansion across all nine Central US Kubernetes clusters, more than doubling capacity. That capacity is already carrying real growth. events.excerpt: What if you could see sound? A Chladni plate uses a speaker and small particles, like sand, to give you a visual representation of sound, and [CrazyScience] shows you how to make one. The plate dates back to 1787, created by the eponymous physicist. Of course, back then, there were no speakers, so the original plate was metal with a violin bow raked across the edges. The modern version uses an ESP32, a speaker, and salt. The patterns depend on the resonance points of the plate. The device has a rotary encoder to tune different frequencies. Check it out in the video below. There’s also an OLED display to show the frequency and patterns. There is also a 3D-printed enclosure. The patterns, of course, depend on standing waves. We aren’t sure that there’s any practical value for it, but we like the way it looks. This isn’t the first time we’ve talked about Chladni . Visualizing things before the CRT was interesting, to say the least.
events.headline: Watch That Sound: Your Own Chladni Plate
